name: Archaeological Park and Ruins of Quirigua
description: Quiriguá is a Maya city in the lowland jungle of Izabal, southeastern Guatemala, beside the Motagua River. Its buildings are modest, but its Great Plaza is filled with huge carved stone monuments, including the tallest stele the Maya ever raised. Here, in 738, King K'ak' Tiliw defeated and sacrificed Copán's ruler, freeing Quiriguá from its powerful neighbour.
